_note: priority: core = tested at nearly every firm; high = tested at many; medium = situational; low = rarely tested for TRADER roles (skip unless role is research). Keywords are lowercase regex fragments matched against course documents. Priorities come from candidate-reported sources (see references/firms.md), not official specs.

topics.name: Mental arithmetic speed
topics.course_overlap: Almost never taught in courses; always needs separate drilling.

topics.name: Expected value, variance, linearity of expectation
Common distributions and moments (binomial, geometric, Poisson, normal, exponential, uniform)
Random walks, gambler's ruin, Markov chains, recursion / first-step analysis
Betting and EV games (coin/dice/card games, bet sizing, Kelly)
topics.course_overlap: Courses rarely cover this as a game; practise out loud.

topics.name: Market making (bid/ask, spread, inventory, adverse selection, updating quotes)
topics.course_overlap: Only microstructure/finance courses touch this; the interview skill is a live game and needs deliberate practice.

topics.name: Game theory (Nash, zero-sum, mixed strategies, AKQ/poker, Penney's game, pirate game)
topics.note: Heaviest at SIG (poker) and DRW; lighter elsewhere.

topics.name: Options & derivatives basics (payoffs, put-call parity, Greeks, Black-Scholes intuition, no-arbitrage)
topics.note: Optiver, IMC, SIG, Akuna weigh this more. Intuition > derivation.

topics.name: Statistics (hypothesis tests, regression, estimation, Bayesian updating)
topics.note: Core for researcher roles; for trader roles mostly CLT/LLN, Bayesian updating and basic regression intuition.

topics.name: Linear algebra & calculus (eigenvalues, PCA, optimisation, integrals)
topics.note: Mostly a prerequisite for research roles; light for traders.

topics.name: Programming (Python/numpy/pandas; C++ for HRT/IMC-type roles; algorithms)
topics.note: Light for pure trader roles at some firms; stronger at HRT, IMC, and research tracks.

topics.name: Stochastic calculus (Brownian motion, Ito, Girsanov, PDE derivation of Black-Scholes)
topics.note: Usually NOT needed for trader intern/grad interviews; useful for quant research or bank derivatives desks.

topics.name: Machine learning & time series (ARIMA, GARCH, regularisation, tree models)
topics.note: Research-track; skip for trader prep unless the job post says otherwise.

topics.name: Markets awareness (what's moving, ETFs, rates, how exchanges work, your own trading views)
topics.note: Firms like Optiver/IMC/SIG ask about decision-making and curiosity, not textbook finance.
